extracted.intended_audience: GAP users; computational group theorists and mathematicians using GAP
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP functions dealing with subgroups, subgroup series, group properties, and related constructions; defines behavior, mathematical meaning, and example usage of each routine. Intended to guide users in computing and reasoning about finite groups in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCore
rubrics_metrics.description: The p-core of G is the largest normal p-subgroup of G; it is the core of a Sylow p-subgroup of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PCore(G,p). Examples: PCore(DicyclicGroup(12),2) returns Group([ y3 ]). It equals Core(g,SylowSubgroup(g,p)).

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalClosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The normal closure of U in G is the smallest normal subgroup of the closure of G and U which contains U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: NormalClosure(G, U) or NormalClosure(G, list) where list is a list of group elements. Examples show NormalClosure(g,Subgroup(g,[(1,2,3)])) and NormalClosure(g,[(1,2,3)]).

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalIntersection
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the intersection of G and U, assuming that G is normalized by U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: NormalIntersection(G,U). Works faster than Intersection but will not produce the intersection if G is not normalized by U. Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplementClassesRepresentatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a set of representatives for the conjugacy classes of complements of a normal subgroup N in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complements intersect trivially with N and together with N generate G. Methods available only when N or G/N is solvable. Usage: ComplementClassesRepresentatives(G,N). Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoComplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Info class for the complement routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: InfoComplement. (An info class controlling verbosity/logging for complement routines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the trivial subgroup of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: TrivialSubgroup(G). Example: TrivialSubgroup(g) returns Group(()).

rubrics_metrics.name: CommutatorSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the subgroup generated by all commutators [g,h]=g^{-1}h^{-1}gh for g in G and h in H, i.e., ⟨[g,h] | g∈G, h∈H⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CommutatorSubgroup(G,H). Example and Size(last) demonstration provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: DerivedSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The derived subgroup G' of G is the subgroup generated by all commutators of pairs of elements of G; it is normal and G/G' is the largest abelian factor group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: DerivedSubgroup(G). Example shows equality to an explicitly listed subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: CommutatorLength
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the minimal number n such that each element in the derived subgroup can be written as a product of at most n commutators of elements in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CommutatorLength(G). Example: CommutatorLength(g) returns 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: FittingSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fitting subgroup of G is its largest nilpotent normal subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: FittingSubgroup(G). Example shows returned subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: FrattiniSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The Frattini subgroup of G is the intersection of all maximal subgroups of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: FrattiniSubgroup(G). Example: FrattiniSubgroup(g) may return trivial group.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrefrattiniSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a Prefrattini subgroup of the finite solvable group G: a subgroup that covers each Frattini chief factor and is contained (up to conjugacy) in conjugate maximal subgroups; their intersection is the Frattini subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PrefrattiniSubgroup(G). Examples show properties: size, nilpotency, relation with Core and FrattiniSubgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: PerfectResiduum
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfect residuum is the smallest normal subgroup of G that has a solvable factor group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PerfectResiduum(G). Example: PerfectResiduum(SymmetricGroup(5)) returns Alt([1..5]).

rubrics_metrics.name: SolvableRadical
rubrics_metrics.description: The solvable radical of G is the largest solvable normal subgroup of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SolvableRadical(G). Examples show return type and Size(rad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Socle
rubrics_metrics.description: The socle of G is the subgroup generated by all minimal normal subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Socle(G). Example: Socle(g) returns a subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: SupersolvableResiduum
rubrics_metrics.description: The supersolvable residuum of G is its smallest normal subgroup N such that G/N is supersolvable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SupersolvableResiduum(G). Example equality shown for a sample group.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRump
rubrics_metrics.description: For a prime p, the p-rump PRump(G,p) is the subgroup G' G^p (the subgroup generated by derived subgroup and pth powers); unless equal to G, it equals the second term of the p-central series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PRump(G,p). Examples compare with PCentralSeries(G,p)[2].

rubrics_metrics.name: SylowSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a Sylow p-subgroup of finite group G: a p-subgroup whose index in G is coprime to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SylowSubgroup(G,p). Computed via SylowSubgroupOp. Example: SylowSubgroup(SymmetricGroup(4),2).

rubrics_metrics.name: SylowComplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a Sylow p-complement: subgroup U of order coprime to p with index [G:U] a p-power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SylowComplement(G,p). Methods exist only if G is solvable; error if G not solvable. Example: SylowComplement(g,3).

rubrics_metrics.name: HallSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a P-Hall subgroup for a set P of primes: subgroup whose order is divisible only by primes in P and whose index is coprime to all primes in P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: HallSubgroup(G,P). If G solvable, always returns a subgroup; if not solvable may return subgroup, list of representatives, or fail. Examples illustrate returned forms and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SylowSystem
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sylow system of G is a set of Sylow subgroups such that every pair commutes as subgroups; they exist only for solvable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SylowSystem(G). Returns fail if G not solvable. Example shows returned list and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplementSystem
rubrics_metrics.description: A complement system is a set of Hall p'-subgroups (one for each subset of prime factors omitting exactly one prime) where every pair commutes; exists only for solvable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ComplementSystem(G). Returns fail if G not solvable. Example and sizes shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: HallSystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list containing one Hall P-subgroup for each set P of prime divisors of |G|. Hall systems exist only for solvable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: HallSystem(G). Returns fail if G not solvable. Example shows list and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omega
rubrics_metrics.description: For a p-group G, Ω_n(G) = ⟨ g ∈ G | g^{p^n} = 1 ⟩; default n = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Omega(G,p[,n]). Example: Omega(h,2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agemo
rubrics_metrics.description: For a p-group G, ℧_n(G) = ⟨ g^{p^n} | g ∈ G ⟩; default n = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Agemo(G,p[,n]). Examples: Agemo(h,2) and Agemo(h,2,2) shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: IsCyclic(G) returns true if G can be generated by one element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can compute a minimal generating set consisting of only one element using MinimalGeneratingSet. Usage: IsCyclic(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsElementaryAbelian
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: G is elementary abelian if it is commutative and there is a prime p such that the order of each element divides p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsElementaryAbelian(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNilpotentGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: A group is nilpotent if its lower central series reaches the trivial subgroup in a finite number of steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsNilpotentGroup(G). See LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup for definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: NilpotencyClassOfGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute: Nilpotency class of a nilpotent group G is the number of steps in the lower central series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: NilpotencyClassOfGroup(G). If G is not nilpotent an error is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPerfectGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: A group is perfect if it equals its derived subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPerfectGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSolvableGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: G is solvable if the derived series reaches the trivial subgroup in a finite number of steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsSolvableGroup(G). For finite groups solvability = polycyclic; note infinite solvable groups need not be polycyclic.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPolycyclicGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: G is polycyclic if it has a subnormal series with cyclic factors; for finite groups this is equivalent to solvability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPolycyclicGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSupersolvableGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: A finite group is supersolvable if it has a normal series with cyclic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsSupersolvableGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMonomialGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: A finite group is monomial if every irreducible complex character is induced from a linear character of a subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsMonomialGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSimpleGroup / IsNonabelianSimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties: IsSimpleGroup(G) returns true if G is nontrivial and has no nontrivial normal subgroups. IsNonabelianSimpleGroup(G) is true if simple and not abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsSimpleGroup(G) and IsNonabelianSimpleGroup(G). Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAlmostSimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: G is almost simple if there exists a nonabelian simple group S such that G is isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut(S) that contains all inner automorphisms; equivalently G has a unique minimal normal subgroup N which is nonabelian simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: almost simple excludes extensions of groups of prime order; a nonabelian simple group is almost simple. Usage and examples shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsQuasisimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Property: G is quasisimple if G is perfect and G/Z(G) is simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsQuasisimpleGroup(G). Examples: AlternatingGroup(5) true, SymmetricGroup(5) false, SL(2,5) true.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite simple group G (or a positive integer n), returns a record with components name, shortname, series, and possibly parameter describing the isomorphism type of G; for n returns fail if n is not the order of a finite simple group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields: name (strings), shortname (compatible with CTblLib/AtlasRep), series (codes like 'A','L','B', etc.) and parameter. If multiple simple groups have the same order, record may contain only name listing possibilities. Examples and mapping of series codes given.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs an instance of the specified nonabelian simple group by ATLAS-style name and optional parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SimpleGroup(id[,param]). Intelligence applied to parsing is limited; AtlasRep package might be needed for some groups. Examples: SimpleGroup("M(23)"), SimpleGroup("PSL",3,5).

rubrics_metrics.name: SimpleGroupsIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an iterator over all nonabelian simple groups, starting at order start up to order end (default up to 10^27), with option NOPSL2 to omit PSL2(q) groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SimpleGroupsIterator([start[,end]]). Examples demonstrate iterating and listing groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallSimpleGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the i-th simple group of given order in the stored list, in a small-degree permutation representation, or fail if none exists. i defaults to 1. All simple groups of order < 10^6 are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SmallSimpleGroup(order[,i]). Examples shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of all nonabelian simple groups whose order lies in the specified range, given in small-degree permutation representations, sorted by ascending order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups(orders). Example shows list for [1..1000000].

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether G can be generated by a finite number of generators (existence statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup(G). Note: property is mainly used to obtain finiteness conditions; proving existence does not necessarily produce generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks whether U is a subset of a locally finite group (every finitely generated subgroup is finite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup(U). Used to check whether finite generation implies finiteness in given context (e.g., permutation groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if G is a p-group: every element order is a power of a prime p. For finite groups this means order is 1 or a prime power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPGroup(G). Note that p-groups can be infinite and need not be nilpotent then. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPowerfulPGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite p-group G is powerful if [G,G] ≤ G^p for odd p, or [G,G] ≤ G^4 for p=2. Returns true if G is powerful (trivial group returns true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPowerfulPGroup(G). Note: G^p denotes first Agemo subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegularPGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite p-group G is regular if for all a,b in G, a^p b^p = (ab)^p c where c lies in the derived subgroup of ⟨a,b⟩. Returns true if G is regular (trivial group returns true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsRegularPGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimePGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is a nontrivial p-group, returns the prime p; if G is trivial returns fail; otherwise issues an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PrimePGroup(G). Caution: avoid code that assumes PrimePGroup(g) is integer without checking IsPGroup(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: PClassPGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The p-class of a p-group G is the length of its lower p-central series (PCentralSeries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PClassPGroup(G). Errors if G not a p-group.

rubrics_metrics.name: RankPGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: For a p-group G, returns the minimal size of a generating system (the rank).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: RankPGroup(G). Errors if G not a p-group. Examples show PClassPGroup and RankPGroup usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPSolvable
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite group is p-solvable if every chief factor either has order not divisible by p or is solvable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPSolvable(G,p). This is parameter-dependent and not a GAP property in the attribute sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPNilpotent
rubrics_metrics.description: A group is p-nilpotent if it possesses a normal p-complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IsPNilpotent(G,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianInvariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the abelian invariants (primary decomposition) of the commutator factor group G/G', given as a list of prime-powers or zeros describing direct product decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: AbelianInvariants(G). See IndependentGeneratorsOfAbelianGroup to obtain generators. Examples shown including infinite factor using 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponent
rubrics_metrics.description: The exponent e of G is the lcm of orders of its elements; the smallest integer e such that g^e = 1 for all g in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Exponent(G). Example: Exponent(g) returns 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: EulerianFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: EulerianFunction(G,n) returns the number of n-tuples (g1,...,gn) of elements of G that generate G (elements need not be distinct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation: φ_n(G) in literature; φ_n(G)/|Aut(G)| = d_n(G). If Library of Tables of Marks covers G, EulerianFunctionByTom may be used. Usage and example: EulerianFunction(g,2) returns 432.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChiefSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: ChiefSeries(G) returns a chief series: a series of normal subgroups of G that cannot be refined further (no normal subgroup between consecutive terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ChiefSeries(G). Returns one possible chief series (not necessarily unique). Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChiefSeriesThrough
rubrics_metrics.description: ChiefSeriesThrough(G,l) returns a chief series going through the normal subgroups in list l (list must be normal subgroups, contained in each other, sorted by descending size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ChiefSeriesThrough(G,l). Returns one chief series incorporating the given normals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChiefSeriesUnderAction
rubrics_metrics.description: ChiefSeriesUnderAction(H,G) returns a series of normal subgroups of G invariant under H such that series cannot be refined; requires G ≤ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ChiefSeriesUnderAction(H,G). Returns one such series.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubnormalSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: SubnormalSeries(G,U) returns a subnormal series descending from G to a subnormal subgroup V ≥ U; if U is subnormal then V = U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: SubnormalSeries(G,U). Example shows returned list.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompositionSeries / CompositionSeriesThrough
rubrics_metrics.description: CompositionSeries(G) returns a composition series: a subnormal series which cannot be refined. CompositionSeriesThrough(G,normals) returns a composition series that incorporates the listed normal subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CompositionSeries(G) or CompositionSeriesThrough(G,normals). Returns one possible composition series.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayCompositionSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays a composition series of G in a readable way, identifying the simple factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: DisplayCompositionSeries(G). Example shows formatted output with sizes and factor names.

rubrics_metrics.name: DerivedSeriesOfGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The derived series is obtained by U_{i+1} = U'_i and stops if U_i is perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: DerivedSeriesOfGroup(G). Example shows List(DerivedSeriesOfGroup(g),Size).

rubrics_metrics.name: DerivedLength
rubrics_metrics.description: The derived length of G is the number of steps in the derived series (series length minus 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: DerivedLength(G). Example: DerivedLength(g) returns 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementaryAbelianSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a series of normal subgroups of G with elementary abelian factors; returns fail if group is not solvable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variants: ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps (tries to make steps large) and ElementaryAbelianSeries(list) constructs series through given normals. Example shows List(ElementaryAbelianSeries(g),Size).

rubrics_metrics.name: InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: For solvable G and list of automorphisms morph, finds a normal series with elementary abelian factors invariant under each automorphism in morph. Optionally contains a normal subgroup N invariant under morph. Prefers large steps unless fine=true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries(G, morph[, N[, fine]]). No argument validity tests are performed. Example demonstrates using a group homomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The lower central series is defined by U_{i+1} := [G, U_i]; it is a central series of normal subgroups and Ui is contained in the i-th step subgroup of any central series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The upper central series is defined by U_i/U_{i+1} := Z(G/U_{i+1}); it is a central series of normal subgroups and Ui contains every i-th step subgroup of a central series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCentralSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: The p-central series of G is defined by U1 := G, Ui := [G, U_{i-1}] U_{i-1}^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: PCentralSeries(G,p). Example compares PRump with PCentralSeries(g,2)[2] and shows List(PCentralSeries(g,2),StructureDescription).

rubrics_metrics.name: JenningsSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: For a p-group G, returns its Jennings series: G1 = G and for i ≥ 0, G_{i+1} = [G_i, G] G_p^j where j is the smallest integer > i/p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: JenningsSeries(G). Example demonstrates series for a small p-group.

rubrics_metrics.name: DimensionsLoewyFactors
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the dimensions of the factors of the Loewy series of G via the JenningsSeries without computing the Loewy series itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: DimensionsLoewyFactors(G). References [HB82] for definition. Example shows a long list of dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AscendingChain
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes an ascending chain of subgroups from U to G (list from U to G), trying to make the links small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: AscendingChain(G,U). Options: refineIndex bounds refinements; cheap=true limits heuristic searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntermediateGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Tries to find a subgroup E with G > E > U. If U is maximal in G returns fail. Done by finding minimal blocks for action of G on right cosets of U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IntermediateGroup(G,U).

rubrics_metrics.name: IntermediateSubgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of all subgroups of G that properly contain U (all subgroups between G and U) as a record with component subgroups and inclusions listing maximality relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: IntermediateSubgroups(G,U). Inclusions are given as [i,j] pairs where indices refer to positions in the subgroups list; 0 and 1+Length(subgroups) denote U and G.

rubrics_metrics.name: StructuralSeriesOfGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The structural series of a finite group G is a descending series of characteristic subgroups going through the derived series of the solvable radical of G, refined into elementary abelian factors, as well as the socle and the Pker of the radical factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: StructuralSeriesOfGroup(G). Example shows List(StructuralSeriesOfGroup(gp),Size).

rubrics_metrics.name: NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a homomorphism from G to another group whose kernel is the normal subgroup N; GAP selects an image group to make computations efficient. The homomorphism returned is not necessarily surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup(G,N) or NC variant that does not check normality. Use ImagesSource instead of Range to get a group isomorphic to the factor group. Examples show mapping and Sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: FactorGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the image of NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup(G,N) (provided for compatibility); FactorGroupNC omits normality check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: FactorGroup(G,N) or FactorGroupNC(G,N). Note recommendation: obtain the NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup if connection between group and factor is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: CommutatorFactorGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the commutator factor group G/G' of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CommutatorFactorGroup(G). Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: MaximalAbelianQuotient
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an epimorphism from G onto the maximal abelian quotient of G; kernel is the derived subgroup G'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: MaximalAbelianQuotient(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: HasAbelianFactorGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether G/N is abelian without explicitly constructing the factor group or testing whether N is normal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: HasAbelianFactorGroup(G,N). Example: HasAbelianFactorGroup(g,n) returns false; applied to DerivedSubgroup can return true.

rubrics_metrics.name: HasElementaryAbelianFactorGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether G/N is elementary abelian without explicitly constructing the factor group or testing whether N is normal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: HasElementaryAbelianFactorGroup(G,N).

rubrics_metrics.name: CentralizerModulo
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the full preimage of the centralizer C_{G/N}(elm · N) in G (without necessarily constructing the factor group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CentralizerModulo(G,N,elm). Example: CentralizerModulo(g,n,(1,2)) returns a subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConjugacyClassSubgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates the conjugacy class of subgroups of G with representative U; returns an external set with operations like Representative, ActingDomain, StabilizerOfExternalSet, AsList.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ConjugacyClassSubgroups(G,U). Note: the [] list access to select class elements is obsolescent and ClassElementLattice should be used instead.
